claim: America funds Israel's war. Our money buys the bombs.

answer: Part of this is true. The US has given Israel about $174 billion in current dollars, the largest cumulative total since World War II (Egypt: over $90 billion, historical dollars). Under a 2016 agreement the US pledged $38 billion for 2019 to 2028: $3.3 billion a year in military grants and $500 million a year for missile defence. It is a pledge, not a law; Congress votes each year. In April 2024 Congress appropriated $3.5 billion in grants and $5.2 billion for missile defence, in a $95 billion package that gave Ukraine $60.8 billion. In the war's first year, Brown's Costs of War project counts at least $17.9 billion in approved security assistance, a partial figure. Left out: two counts put US grants at 14 to 20 percent of Israel's defence budget. On 3 November 2026 President Trump said the aid would stop by year end; Congress controls the money.

could_not_verify: A single audited figure for US arms actually delivered since October 2023: the $17.9 billion is the Costs of War project's count of approved assistance and the authors call it partial; the AP says full shipments cannot be tracked as Ukraine's can.
The Israeli Ministry of Defense statement of 90,000 tons: the original and the Times of Israel article could not be fetched; it is quoted via the CRS report and the CFR.
Three reliable sources for fact 2 (largest cumulative recipient): the CRS is a government source; the CFR and one local news report that cites the CFR are the only independent ones.

Three reliable sources for fact 3 (Egypt and Ukraine): the Egypt figure rests on the CRS only; Ukraine rests on the CFR and NPR. The CRS Israel and Egypt totals use historical dollars; the CFR Ukraine figure counts war-related spending, including US operations in Europe, so it is not like-for-like.
Three reliable sources for fact 4 (share of Israel's defence budget): only the CRS (14 percent, grants only) and the CFR (about 20 percent, all aid, 'reportedly').
Congress's reaction to the 3 November 2026 announcement, and whether any funding has changed; the pages read are from the day it was announced.
Whether $26.4 billion (CBS) or $26 billion (VOA) is the right total for Israel-related items in the April 2024 law; the card gives the law's line items instead.

Whether the 3 November 2026 announcement is more than a statement: Al Jazeera says it was not clear what form of aid Trump meant, and TWZ quotes Politico that no formal document was submitted by the prime minister's office. Fact 6 and the last sentence of the answer say only what he said, and rest on three independent outlets (TWZ, Al Jazeera, Reuters via Al-Monitor), all reporting one television interview.

A source on the card that puts the case that the aid is defensive or is spent mostly in the United States: 'contested' holds the critics' side only (the other side is on era8-where-it-goes-and-who-objects).
not_claimed: This card does not say the aid is right or wrong, or that it should continue.
It does not say that any specific US-made weapon caused any specific death; that is a question for the incident-level records.
It does not say the aid pays for the whole of Israel's war; it gives amounts and the share of the Israeli defence budget that two sources report (about 14 to 20 percent before the war).
It does not say Congress or the president has decided the future of the aid after November 2026.

answer_claims.says: The US has given Israel about $174 billion in current dollars, the largest cumulative total since World War II (Egypt: over $90 billion, historical dollars).
Under a 2016 agreement the US pledged $38 billion for 2019 to 2028: $3.3 billion a year in military grants and $500 million a year for missile defence.
It is a pledge, not a law; Congress votes each year.
In April 2024 Congress appropriated $3.5 billion in grants and $5.2 billion for missile defence, in a $95 billion package that gave Ukraine $60.8 billion.
In the war's first year, Brown's Costs of War project counts at least $17.9 billion in approved security assistance, a partial figure.
Left out: two counts put US grants at 14 to 20 percent of Israel's defence budget.
On 3 November 2026 President Trump said the aid would stop by year end; Congress controls the money.

skeptic.notes: Round 1. Quotes are on their pages and in context. Dollar figures checked: $38bn/$33bn/$5bn pledged for FY2019-2028 (CRS: 'subject to congressional appropriation'); $174bn current dollars (CRS, May 2025) against CFR $300bn inflation-adjusted; April 2024 law lines read in the law ($3.5bn to 30 Sep 2025, $4bn, $1.2bn, $5.2bn to 30 Sep 2026): appropriated, not delivered (text now says so); $17.9bn is Costs of War's count of approved aid, which AP calls 'spent' (the card keeps 'approved'); the CFR $16.3bn covers a longer period (to FY2025) and was set beside it as if comparable (fixed in text). Fixed: fact 2 called the CFR's $196bn 'the war in Ukraine' but it includes Operation Atlantic Resolve; fact 3 said 'before the war' for the CRS's 14%, which the CRS bases on a January 2024 Jane's figure and does not date. 3 November 2026: three independent, readable outlets carry it (TWZ, Al Jazeera, Reuters via Al-Monitor), so the answer may say 'Trump said'; kept as a statement only, and not as policy (all three report one interview; Al Jazeera says it was unclear what aid he meant). Strongest objection from the critics' side: the card gives their position only as two quotes and never states the strongest version (heard[0] is Sanders on starvation, not on weapons; should-fix). From the pro-aid side: contested is critics only and carries no holder of 'the aid is defensive' (should-fix; a source is needed). Only 7 of 16 facts across the two chapter 8 cards have three reliable sources; here facts 1 to 3 do not (CFR and WJLA, which cites the CFR, are one voice). Kinds checked: CRS and White House government; the law primary. Status stays draft.

citer.notes: Removed: 'since 1946' (the CRS quote says 'to date'), 'the most of any country' (reworded to the CRS's 'largest cumulative recipient'), and 'most of the money is spent in the US, and the US Congress sets conditions' (no fact on this card says either; they sit on the sibling card). 'Part of this is true' is a summary tied to the facts for and against. 'In April 2024 Congress added' changed to 'appropriated'. 'at least $17.9 billion in military aid was approved' now credits the Costs of War count and calls it partial. Added one sentence that the card's own fact 3 supports (14 to 20 percent of the defence budget).
